gloss: border, boundary; territory within it; set bounds
summary: The line where one people's or one man's land ends and another's begins, and the land enclosed by it. גְּבוּל, about 240 times, is the border drawn round the land of Canaan and each tribe's portion (Num 34; Jos 15–19; Ezk 47–48), a neighbour's boundary that may not be moved (Deu 19:14; Pro 22:28), the territory inside the border (Exo 10:4; 13:7), the bound Yahweh set for the sea (Psa 104:9; Jer 5:22), and the rim of the altar (Ezk 43:13). The verb borders on a place or sets bounds round it, as round Sinai (Exo 19:12, 23). In the Peshitta the same letters are the verb “knead, form”, used of the potter's clay and of Adam “formed first” (Rom 9:20; 1Ti 2:13); how that sense and “border” belong together is not understood.

words.gloss: border, boundary; territory; boundary mark; rim
words.summary: About 240 times, above all in the border lists of Numbers 34, Joshua 13–19 and Ezekiel 47–48. It is both the line (“the border went up…”, Jos 15:6–8) and what it encloses (“within all your borders”, Exo 13:7). Psa 78:54 sets “the border of his holiness” beside “this mountain that his right hand acquired”, the pairing behind the Ugaritic and Arabic word for mountain.

senses.definition: The line where a land, a tribe's portion or a people's country ends, described by the places it runs through.

evidence.note: “Your south side shall be from the wilderness of Zin … and your south border shall be from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.”
“The border went up the valley of Ben Hinnom to the shoulder of the Jebusite … and the border went up to the head of the hill.”
“This shall be your land according to its borders all around.”
“The border of Manasseh was from Asher to Mikmethath.”
“We are in Kadesh, a city at the end of your border.”
“You are passing over today the border of Moab, Ar.”
“The border of the Canaanite was from Sidon … to Gaza.”
“This is the border by which you shall inherit the land for the twelve tribes of Israel.”
“All the men of your covenant have sent you to the border.”

senses.definition: The land enclosed by a border: a country, a tribe's portion or a city's land, especially with בְּכָל “in all your territory”.

evidence.note: “Behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your border”: into the land of Egypt.
“No leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders.”
The same of the Passover: no leaven “in all your border seven days”.
Yahweh struck “Ashdod and its borders”.
“Send messengers into all the border of Israel.”
They sought a fair girl “in all the border of Israel”.
Hazael struck them “in all the border of Israel”.
“He brought them to the border of his holiness, this mountain that his right hand acquired”: the land as Yahweh's holy territory, set in parallel with a mountain.
“He makes your border peace.”
“Destruction and breaking within your borders”, set beside “in your land”.
“Your sons shall return to their own border.”
“In the border of Israel I will judge you.”
The Assyrian “treads within our border”.
“In Bethlehem and all its borders (ὅρια)”: the territory round the town.

senses.definition: The boundary of a man's inheritance, marked on the ground, which the law forbids moving.

evidence.note: “You shall not move your neighbour's border, which the men of old set (גָּבְלוּ), in your inheritance.”
“Cursed is he who moves his neighbour's border.”
“Do not move the ancient border that your fathers made.”
“Do not move the ancient border, and do not enter the fields of the fatherless.”
“Yahweh will tear down the house of the proud, but he will set up the border of the widow.”
“The princes of Judah are like those who move a border.”

senses.gloss: bound, limit (of the sea, of the waters)
senses.definition: The limit Yahweh set for the sea and the waters, which they do not pass.

evidence.note: “You set a border they cannot pass; they will not return to cover the earth.”
“I have placed the sand as a border for the sea, an eternal decree, and it does not pass over it.”
Of light and darkness: “that you should take it to its border”.

senses.gloss: rim, edge, ledge (of the altar, a wall)
senses.definition: In the measurements of Ezekiel's temple, the raised rim or ledge round the altar, and a low barrier; in Isaiah, the enclosing wall of the city.

evidence.note: “Its border to its lip around is one span.”
“The border around it half a cubit.”
Blood put “on the border round about”.
“A border before the chambers, one cubit.”
“All your border of stones of delight”, with battlements and gates: the city's enclosing wall.

evidence.note: “In Bethlehem and in all its borders (ὁρίοις).”
Capernaum “in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali”, in the fulfilment of Isa 8:23–9:1.
“Through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.”

parallels.note: “The border of his holiness” and “this mountain”.

phrases.gloss: and the border shall be (in the border lists)

words.summary: Ten times, nearly always plural, in the same senses as גְּבוּל: a land “according to its borders”, the bounds of peoples and of the earth, and the edge of a field.

senses.definition: The borders of a land or of the peoples, which Yahweh set and the Assyrian boasted he had removed.

evidence.note: “The land of Canaan according to its borders.”
“They finished inheriting the land according to its borders.”
“When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance … he set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.”
Paul at Athens: God made every nation from one blood and “determined … the bounds (ὁροθεσίας) of their habitation”, the thought of Deu 32:8.
“You set all the borders of the earth; summer and winter, you formed them.”
The king of Assyria: “I have removed the borders of peoples, and plundered their treasures.”
“They move borders; they seize flocks.”
The ploughman sows “spelt at its border”: the edge of the field.

evidence.locator: Deu.32.8, גְּבֻלֹת → ὅρια; ὅριον renders גְּבוּלָה ×6

words.summary: Five times, made from the noun: in the qal, to border on a place or to mark out a boundary; in the hiphil, to set bounds round the people and the mountain at Sinai.

stems.gloss: border on; mark out a boundary

senses.gloss: border on, be the border of; set a boundary
senses.definition: Of a river or a city, to be the border of a land or lie next to it; of men, to mark out a boundary.

evidence.note: “The Jordan borders it on the east side.”
“And Hamath also, which borders on it; Tyre and Sidon.”
“Your neighbour's border, which the men of old set (גָּבְלוּ).”

senses.definition: To fix a limit round a people or a place so that none crosses it: round the people, and round Mount Sinai to keep it holy.

evidence.note: “You shall set bounds for the people round about, saying, Take heed not to go up the mountain or touch its edge.”
“You warned us, saying, Set bounds round the mountain and sanctify it.”
Of the same bounds: “If even a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned” (Exo 19:13).

evidence.locator: Exo.19.12, הִגְבַּלְתָּ → ἀφοριεῖς; Exo.19.23, הַגְבֵּל → ἀφόρισαι

evidence.note: “Come out from among them and be separate (ἀφορίσθητε)”, after Isa 52:11.

words.summary: Twice, of the gold chains of the high priest's breastpiece, “chains of גַּבְלֻת, cord work”. The sense “twisted” is taken from the cord work beside it; the word's link to the root's sense is not clear, and it may instead mean “at the ends”, the ends of the breastpiece where the chains were fastened (Exo 28:22–25).

senses.definition: Describing the gold chains made as cord work for the breastpiece.

evidence.note: “Chains of גַּבְלֻת, cord work (מַעֲשֵׂה עֲבֹת), of pure gold.”
The same, as made.
The chains are put on the two rings “at the ends (קְצוֹת) of the breastpiece”.

words.gloss: twisted work (?) or at the ends (?)
words.summary: Once, of the two gold chains of the ephod: “מִגְבָּלֹת you shall make them, cord work”. It may be a noun “twisted things”, or the preposition מִן with גְּבֻלֹת, “at the ends”. As with גַּבְלֻת, the link to the root's sense is not clear.

senses.definition: Describing the two gold chains made as cord work for the settings of the ephod.

evidence.note: “Two chains of pure gold, מִגְבָּלֹת you shall make them, cord work.”

words.summary: The gentilic of גְּבַל, Byblos: its land, which Israel did not take, and its men, who cut stone for Solomon's house.

senses.definition: A man of Gebal, or the land of Gebal.

evidence.note: “The land of the Gebalite, and all Lebanon”, among the land that remained.
“Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites cut and prepared the timber and the stones.”

words.gloss: Gebal, Byblos, on the Phoenician coast
words.summary: The seaport north of Sidon whose own inscriptions call it gbl. How the name comes from the root is not shown; it may be “border” or “mountain”, from the hills behind it. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: The Phoenician city whose skilled men caulked the ships of Tyre.

evidence.note: “The elders of Gebal and her wise men were in you, repairing your seams.”

words.gloss: Gebal, a region named among Israel's enemies
words.summary: Once, in a list of peoples allied against Israel, between Edom and Moab and Ammon and Amalek. Where it lay is not stated; set with Edom and Amalek it is taken as the hill country south of the Dead Sea, and the name read as “hill country”, as Sabaean gblt and Arabic jabal, which rests on little. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: A people or land in league with Edom, Moab, Ammon and Amalek against Israel.

evidence.note: “Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre.”
“The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarenes.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb, of kneading clay and of God's forming of man. Its link to the Hebrew “border” is not understood; Arabic has both meanings under one root (jabal “mountain”, jabala “create, form”).

senses.definition: To work clay or earth into a mass or a shape; of God, to form a man as a potter forms a vessel.

evidence.note: Jesus “spat on the ground and kneaded (וַגְבַל) clay from his spittle” and put it on the blind man's eyes.
“Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it (לְדַגְבְּלָהּ), Why did you form me (גְּבַלְתָּנִי) thus?” after Isa 29:16; 45:9.

senses.definition: To be formed, of Adam made by God.

evidence.note: “For Adam was formed (אֶתְגְּבֶל) first, and then Eve”: the Peshitta's word for the forming of Gen 2:7.

words.gloss: lump, mass (of dough or clay); thing formed
words.summary: The Peshitta's word for the potter's lump of clay and the lump of dough that a little leaven leavens; in Rom 9:20 the thing formed.

senses.definition: A kneaded mass of clay or dough; that which has been formed.

evidence.note: “Has not the potter authority over his clay, to make from the one lump one vessel for honour and one for dishonour?”
“A little leaven leavens the whole lump.”
“Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump.”
“If the firstfruit is holy, so is the lump.”
“The thing formed (גְּבִילְתָא)” speaking to its maker.

cognates.note: The Hebrew word's own senses: Azatiwada built fortresses “along the borders”, and settled people “in the territory” of his land.

evidence.note: KAI 26 A I 13/14 “along the borders”; KAI 14.18/20 “the territory of <our> land”; Poen. 938 gubulim “district”.

cognates.note: Sabaean. “In town and country”, and “he opened his territory (to irrigation)”: the land within one's bounds, as גְּבוּל “territory”, and hill country, as Arabic jabal.

cognates.note: The Peshitta's “form” of Adam (1Ti 2:13) and of the potter's work (Rom 9:20) is the Arabic of God's creating.

cognates.note: The city's own name in its kings' inscriptions: “Ittobaal son of Ahiram, king of Byblos”.

“Byblos”, KTU 4.338:13, 15; Old Canaanite Gubla, Phoen. gbl, Arabic Jubail.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh drew the borders of the land himself: “I will set your border from the Sea of Reeds to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River” (Exo 23:31), “from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, to the western sea shall be your border” (Deu 11:24; Jos 1:4), and he gave Moses its line on every side (Num 34:2–12). Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt (1Ki 5:1), but only as tributaries; the tribes never held it all. Ezekiel was shown the land divided again: “This is the border by which you shall inherit the land for the twelve tribes of Israel … which I lifted up my hand to give to your fathers” (Ezk 47:13–14), the tribes in bands from north to south, a holy portion in the midst, and a city named “Yahweh is there” (Ezk 48:1–29, 35). No such division has ever been made. The promise to Rachel's children, “your sons shall return to their own border” (Jer 31:17), follows the weeping Matthew quotes at Bethlehem (Jer 31:15; Mat 2:17–18), and Stephen says God gave Abraham no inheritance in the land, “not even a foot's length”, yet promised it to him and to his seed after him (Act 7:5). From the verses: the borders are literal, they were sworn to the fathers, and they have not yet been given as Ezekiel describes, so the promise waits for its fulfilment, when Abraham and his seed inherit the land.

The king of Assyria boasted, “I have removed the borders of peoples” (Isa 10:13), and Yahweh answered that when he had finished his work on Mount Zion he would punish him (Isa 10:12). Micah speaks of a ruler “from Bethlehem Ephrathah … whose goings out are from of old”, who “shall stand and shepherd in the strength of Yahweh … for now he shall be great to the ends of the earth”, and “this one shall be peace, when the Assyrian comes into our land”: “he will deliver us from the Assyrian, when he comes into our land and when he treads within our border” (Mic 5:1–5). Matthew names the ruler from Bethlehem as Christ (Mat 2:4–6). At his first coming Christ did not deliver Israel from an invader within their borders, and his greatness to the ends of the earth is not yet seen. From the verses: the Assyrian of Micah is the invader from the north who comes against the land in the latter days (Ezk 38:8, 15–16), and the deliverance within Israel's border is Christ's at his return.

Psalm 104 tells the making of the earth: “you covered it with the deep like a garment; the waters stood above the mountains. At your rebuke they fled … you set a border they cannot pass; they will not return to cover the earth” (Psa 104:6–9), as on the third day the waters were gathered and the dry land appeared (Gen 1:9). Yahweh made the sand “a border for the sea, an eternal decree” (Jer 5:22). Once the waters did return and cover all the high mountains under the whole heaven (Gen 7:19–20), and after it God promised that the waters would never again become a flood to destroy all flesh, and that summer and winter would not cease (Gen 8:22; 9:11); the psalm says of the same order, “you set all the borders of the earth; summer and winter, you formed them” (Psa 74:17). From the verses: the sea's bounds were set by God's word at the creation, the flood that passed them covered the whole earth, and they now hold by his promise.

“When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided the sons of man, he set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel” (Deu 32:8). Paul tells the Athenians the same: God “made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, and determined their appointed times and the bounds of their habitation, that they should seek the Lord” (Act 17:26–27). From the verses: all nations are of one blood from Adam, and their lands were bounded by God with Israel's inheritance at the centre.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key גבל; no existing entry held any of its words. BDB keys assigned: c.aj.ab גְּבוּל, c.aj.ac גְּבוּלָה, c.aj.af the verb, c.aj.ad גַּבְלֻת, c.aj.ae מִגְבָּלֹת, c.aj.ah גִּבְלִי, c.aj.ag Gebal (Byblos), c.aj.ai Gebal (Psa 83:8). m.ai.bc (מִגְבָּלֹת, a zero-token cross-reference to the same word) is left unassigned, as BDB lists the same occurrence under c.aj.ae. No personal name: TIPNR's Gebal/Gebalite is a Place record only, so no name file. Jos 18:20 and Deu 19:14 have both noun and verb. The Peshitta's גְּבַל “knead, form” (Jhn 9:6; Rom 9:20; 1Ti 2:13, SEDRA lexeme 503) and גְּבִילְתָא “lump” (Rom 9:20–21; 11:16; 1Co 5:6–7; Gal 5:9, lexeme 502) are given as syc words. Leads not cited (the brief forbids Jastrow): Jewish Aramaic and later Hebrew גְּבַל “knead, mix” and the Targums' place גַּבְלָא for Seir; CAL for Old/Imperial Aramaic gbwl (only Anderson–Moser cited); Payne Smith for Syriac beyond SEDRA; Akkadian gablu (argued “mountain”), not found in Oracc; Akkadian gibillu “tinder” (Oracc) is not related. Open questions: (1) whether “border” and the Aramaic-Arabic “knead, form, create” are one root or two homographs: no merged letter decides it, and Arabic keeps both (jabal, jabala) under one root; (2) גַּבְלֻת and מִגְבָּלֹת: “twisted” rests only on the cord work beside them; מִגְבָּלֹת could be מִן + גְּבֻלֹת “at the ends”; Lane's jiblah “a garment good in its thread and weaving” is a faint lead; (3) the location of Gebal in Psa 83:8; (4) the-assyrian and land-promise doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review.
